Exact poem, 14 exact-ten lines, canonical SHA-256 732a900daaf593ea7e1d5ff68b40b0f05614f0df3c395a5526190655ec1f15dc:

We come with letters no one chose to hold,
and pass a single word from hand to hand;
one voice, once said, steps back among the fold,
and no one here can tell where it will land.

A stranger lends the vowel that I lack,
and I return a consonant she needs;
the line, once closed, will never take it back,
the way a furrow holds its scattered seeds.

No signature can claim the lasting thing;
it grew the way a river learns its bed,
from many small surrenders, each a ring
around the word another voice had said.

So do not ask which author you should name;
the song is whole, and no two parts stay same.
